propositions: Source code comments contain unresolvable commit SHAs, run/thread IDs, and dated incident narratives that rot and become stale due to Gerrit rebase-on-submit and retention window expiration.

A detector must identify rot-prone comment patterns: SHA-like hex strings (≥7 chars), run/job/thread IDs (≥8 digits), and date tokens paired with incident verbs (failed, broke, regressed, fixed, caught, observed, hit, crashed, flaked).

All detector-hit sites must be remediated by one of three forms: citing a resolvable ticket/epic/bug ID, dropping the rot-prone token while preserving current-state prose, or replacing SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions findable via git log.

The detector must accept ticket-id citations (4x4 hex-grouped format or word-triple aliases) and honor an 'context: external' escape hatch for vendor-pinned refs, while rejecting false positives like 'bug surfaced' and path-embedded aliases.
CI guard must block reintroduction of rot-prone refs, pass the remediated tree with zero suppressions, and exclude its own unit-test module from tree scans via EXCLUDED_FILES convention.
Detector unit tests must cover acceptor false-accept gotchas (path-embedded aliases, sentence-final aliases) and verify that compliant blocks with ticket citations and durable prose pass cleanly.
